group_assessment.weighting: A pharmacology and metabolomics group mining public NCI-60 omics against alkylating-agent sensitivity; WWOX is one gene in a CNV list. Not a WWOX group. Observation (quartile differences, correlations in public data) is weighted above interpretation (metabolic reprogramming as the resistance mechanism, WWOX as a metabolic regulator), which the paper takes from literature citations, not from a measurement of WWOX.

entries.proposition: The metabolic link of WWOX in this paper is a Discussion sentence that cites literature; WWOX is one of 15 genes differing in copy-number marker intensity between the most sensitive and most resistant quartiles of cell lines, and the metabolic findings of the paper are purine metabolism and related pathways, not WWOX.
entries.snippet: Included in these genes was WWOX, a tumor suppressor gene that has been shown to regulate multiple metabolic processes, including glucose and lipid metabolism [46,47,48,49].

entries.proposition: The CNV statement: 15 genes with more than 5 DIABLO-selected markers; WWOX is among those decreased in the resistant quartile (Q4).
entries.snippet: These genes included those that were increased in copy number intensity (MIR1302-2, MIR3163, CNTN5, MIR1302-9, DDAH1, DISC1FP1, PGR, and TRPC6) and those that were decreased in copy number intensity (MIR1244-3, WWOX, ARL17B, VAT1L, OR4F3, and FRG2) (Table 5).

entries.proposition: Supplemental Table S7: the 22 WWOX markers behind the Table 5 'decreased' call have a mean intensity of about -0.17 in Q4 against about +0.19 in Q1 (range of Q4 means -0.28 to -0.06), i.e. a difference of about 0.35 on a CRMA-type intensity scale averaged over 14-15 lines per quartile; it is a quartile-mean shift in a deletion-prone fragile-site gene, not a per-line deletion call, and the analysis kept only the top 25% of CNV markers by variance and the supervised DIABLO selection (one marker shown as the row).

entries.proposition: Supplemental Table S2: five WWOX transcript probes all show lower expression in the resistant quartile (fold change Q4/Q1 between about 0.73 and 0.95) and none reaches P < 0.05 (smallest P about 0.074); the Table S5 DIABLO first-component loading for WWOX transcript is about -0.34, below the paper's 0.6 cutoff. The copy-number difference is therefore not matched by a significant transcript difference in the same quartiles.

entries.proposition: Supplemental Table S3 (CREAMMIST): WWOX expression correlates NEGATIVELY with IC50 for five alkylating agents (bendamustine rho -0.20, oxaliplatin -0.25 P 7.6e-18, mitomycin -0.23, chlorambucil -0.21, carboplatin -0.22): higher WWOX expression goes with lower IC50 (greater sensitivity), a weak correlation, in the same direction as the copy-number difference. The main text does not state this correlation.

entries.proposition: Figures 3 and 4 (hand reading): the DIABLO plot separates Q1 and Q4 cell lines on component 1 (about 14-15 points each), which a supervised multi-block PLS-DA over about 10^5 variables would be expected to do for 29 samples regardless of biology (INFERENCE; no permutation or held-out test is described); the only metabolic pathway reaching P < 0.05 in the DIABLO joint analysis is purine metabolism (P = 0.0054 with transcripts, 0.012 with proteins), uncorrected; ketone-body synthesis and degradation (P = 0.056) is the next one. No panel names WWOX.

entries.proposition: Figures 1, 2, 5 and 6: heatmap of rank-ordered z-scores of 51 alkylating agents over 58 lines; joint pathways (tight junction, endocytosis, Hippo, adherens junction, sphingolipid signalling) from p < 0.05 features; Pathview purine-metabolism maps; CRISPR-screen pathway hits (Fanconi anaemia, homologous recombination). WWOX appears in none of them; the purine-metabolism maps are the metabolic result and carry no WWOX gene (WWOX is not a metabolic enzyme).
